scope: Forensic audit of Book System versus Prose Project identity, branch/workstream authority, and recent control-state drift. No qualification evidence, code history or exact-SHA receipts were rewritten by this audit.
evidence_reviewed: repository branch inventory and main...literary-prose-engine-001 ancestry comparison

findings.finding: Original Prose handoff explicitly required a separate prose branch/thread and described the Prose system as shared Books infrastructure. This establishes a subordinate development lane, not replacement of the parent Book System.

The Prose bootstrap created LITERARY-PROSE-ENGINE-001 specifically to help System Master Books draft, diagnose, revise, compare and optimize prose, confirming that the engine is built for broader Books/Book-System use.

The Literary Prose master plan correctly scopes itself to literary prose intelligence on branch literary-prose-engine-001. Its technical architecture is not itself evidence of parent Book System authority.

LITERARY-PROSE-CONSOLIDATED-WORKSTREAM-STATE-008 used PRIMARY and CURRENT_RECONCILED_LITERARY_PROSE_PRIMARY_WORKSTREAM_CHAT without an explicit parent-scope qualifier. This allowed a Prose-primary state to be misread as Book-System-primary authority.

Commit 44b3f1c94f3af36e96f79e29efe2dd709ebdcdcd attempted to repair that confusion by inventing BOOK WRITING PROJECT as the top-level project and demoting Prose to a mere component. That repair was incorrect: there are two active projects, Book System parent and Prose Project child.

No dedicated Book-System-named branch existed in the audited branch inventory. Parent project control therefore lacked an explicit repository control surface, increasing dependence on chat labels and subsystem state.

At audit time literary-prose-engine-001 and main were diverged (515 commits ahead and 181 behind from their merge base). Rebase/history rewrite would risk destroying valid work and is unnecessary for authority repair.

root_cause: CONTROL_PLANE_SCOPE_CONFLATION: project, parent system, child project, implementation engine, branch, workstream, capability lane and chat control surface were used interchangeably. The ambiguity allowed a child-project state to become system-wide authority and then caused an overcorrection that collapsed two projects into one.

impact.risk: Book System continuation could be incorrectly routed into a Prose-only blocker, while Prose could lose its valid status as an independently managed child project.

repairs: Create dedicated Book System parent control branch book-system/control-v1.
Establish BOOK-SYSTEM-PROJECT-HIERARCHY-001 as the parent-child authority contract.
Establish an explicit two-project active registry: Book System parent and Prose Project child.
On literary-prose-engine-001, supersede the incorrect BOOK WRITING PROJECT authority record.
On literary-prose-engine-001, create a Prose parent-binding record and State-009 control overlay so PRIMARY is explicitly Prose-project-local.
Preserve all valid technical and qualification evidence; do not rebase or rewrite Prose history.
qualification_effect: NONE. This is a control/identity repair only. Existing qualification authority remains bound to its original exact subject SHA and scope.
